what: inspect_cat() for a single data frame
title: Exploring and visualising categorical features
text: inspect_cat() returns tibble summarising categorical features data frame, combining functionality inspect_imb() table() functions. tibble generated contains columns col_name name categorical column cnt number unique levels feature common common level (see also inspect_imb()) common_pcnt percentage occurrence dominant level levels list tibbles containing frequency tabulations levels example, levels hair_color column Note default, missing (NA) values present, counted distinct categorical level. barplot showing composition categorical column can created using show_plot() function. Note missing values shown grey bars:  argument high_cardinality show_plot() function can used bundle together categories occur small number times. example, combine categories occurring , use:  resulting bundles shown purple.

title: Correlation diagnostics for numeric columns
text: inspect_cor() returns tibble containing Pearson’s correlation coefficient, confidence intervals pp-values pairs numeric columns . function combines functionality cor() cor.test() convenient wrapper. plot showing point estimate confidence intervals printed using show_plot() function. Note intervals straddle null value 0 shown gray:  Notes: tibble sorted descending order absolute coefficient |ρ||\rho|. inspect_cor drops missing values prior calculation correlation coefficient. p_value associated null hypothesis H0:ρ=0H_0: \rho = 0.
code: library(inspectdf) inspect_cor(storms) ## # A tibble: 55 × 7 ##    col_1                        col_2       corr  p_value  lower  upper pcnt_nna ##    <chr>                        <chr>      <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl> ##  1 wind                         category   0.966 0         0.964  0.968     24.5 ##  2 pressure                     wind      -0.928 0        -0.930 -0.926    100   ##  3 pressure                     category  -0.870 0        -0.876 -0.863     24.5 ##  4 hurricane_force_diameter     pressure  -0.768 0        -0.775 -0.760     54.2 ##  5 hurricane_force_diameter     wind       0.720 0         0.711  0.729     54.2 ##  6 tropicalstorm_force_diameter pressure  -0.641 0        -0.651 -0.629     54.2 ##  7 tropicalstorm_force_diameter wind       0.536 0         0.523  0.549     54.2 ##  8 hurricane_force_diameter     tropical…  0.520 0         0.506  0.533     54.2 ##  9 tropicalstorm_force_diameter lat        0.407 0         0.392  0.423     54.2 ## 10 hurricane_force_diameter     category   0.315 5.59e-55  0.279  0.350     11.9 ## # ℹ 45 more rows inspect_cor(storms) %>% show_plot()

title: Correlation diagnostics for numeric columns
text: second dataframe provided, inspect_cor() returns tibble compares correlation coefficients first dataframe second. p_value column contains measure evidence whether two correlation coefficients equal . plot comparison top 20 correlation coefficients:  Notes: Smaller p_value indicates stronger evidence null hypothesis H0:ρ1=ρ2H_0: \rho_1 = \rho_2 indication true correlation coefficients differ. visualisation illustrates significance difference using coloured bar underlay. Coloured bars indicate evidence inequality correlations, gray bars indicate equality. pair features, either coefficient NA, comparison omitted visualisation. significance level can specified using alpha argument inspect_cor(). default alpha = 0.05.

what: inspect_types() for comparing two data frames
title: Exploring dataframe column types
text: illustrate comparison two data frames, create two new data frames randomly sampling rows starwars, dropping columns recoding colums mass character. results assigned objects star_1 star_2: second dataframe provided, inspect_types() returns tibble compares column names types found input data frames. columns cnt_1 cnt_2 contain total number columns type found first second inputs, respectively: columns named list column containing list tibbles. tibble records names columns type. example, numeric column names accessed using: issues column contains list character vectors describing specific points type columns mismatch two data frame inputs. simplest way view issues use unnest() function tidyr package: Finally, can produce simple visualisation showing differences star_1 star_2 using show_plot():
code: # sample 50 rows from `starwars` star_1 <- starwars %>% sample_n(50) # recode the mass column to character star_1$mass <- as.character(star_1$mass) # sample 50 rows from `starwars` and drop the first two columns star_2 <- starwars %>% sample_n(50) %>% select(-1, -2) # compare the column types for star_1 and star_2 x <- inspect_types(star_1, star_2) x ## # A tibble: 4 × 6 ##   type      equal cnt_1 cnt_2 columns           issues    ##   <chr>     <chr> <int> <int> <named list>      <list>    ## 1 character ✘         9     7 <tibble [16 × 2]> <chr [2]> ## 2 list      ✔         3     3 <tibble [6 × 2]>  <NULL>    ## 3 integer   ✘         1     0 <tibble [1 × 2]>  <chr [1]> ## 4 numeric   ✘         1     2 <tibble [3 × 2]>  <chr [1]> # tibble of numeric columns in star_1 or star_2 x$columns$numeric ## # A tibble: 3 × 2 ##   col_name   data_arg ##   <chr>      <chr>    ## 1 birth_year star_1   ## 2 mass       star_2   ## 3 birth_year star_2 library(tidyr) # unnest the issue columns so we can see where the differences are between star_1 and star_2 x %>% select(type, issues) %>% unnest(issues) ## # A tibble: 4 × 2 ##   type      issues                                              ##   <chr>     <chr>                                               ## 1 character star_1::mass ~ character <!> star_2::mass ~ numeric ## 2 character star_1::name ~ character  missing from star_2       ## 3 integer   star_1::height ~ integer  missing from star_2       ## 4 numeric   star_1::mass ~ character <!> star_2::mass ~ numeric # print visualisation of column type comparison inspect_types(star_1, star_2) %>% show_plot()

Defaults 90 plots. label_size Numeric value specifying font size text annotation, applicable. col_palette Integer indicating colour palette use:  0: (default) `ggplot2` color palette, 1: colorblind friendly palette, 2: 80s theme, 3: rainbow theme, 4: mario theme, 5: pokemon theme Arguments plotting inspect_cat() high_cardinality Minimum number occurrences category shown distinct segment plot (inspect_cat() ).  Default 0 - distinct levels shown.  Setting high_cardinality > 0 can speed plot rendering categorical columns contain many near-unique values. label_thresh Minimum occurrence frequency category text label shown.  Smaller values label_thresh show labels less common categories expense increased plot rendering time.  Defaults 0.1. arguments plot_type Experimental.  Integer determining plot type print.  Defaults 1. plot_layout Vector specifying number rows columns plotting grid.  example, 3 rows 2 columns specified plot_layout = c(3, 2).

title: Simple graphical inspection of data frame summaries — show_plot
code: # Load 'starwars' data data("starwars", package = "dplyr")  # Horizontal bar plot for categorical column composition x <- inspect_cat(starwars)  show_plot(x)   # Correlation between numeric columns + confidence intervals x <- inspect_cor(starwars) show_plot(x)   # Bar plot of most frequent category for each categorical column x <- inspect_imb(starwars) show_plot(x)   # Bar plot showing memory usage for each column x <- inspect_mem(starwars) show_plot(x)   # Occurence of NAs in each column ranked in descending order x <- inspect_na(starwars) show_plot(x)   # Histograms for numeric columns x <- inspect_num(starwars) show_plot(x)   # Barplot of column types x <- inspect_types(starwars) show_plot(x)
